results.title: Curacao World Cup 2026: Fixtures, manager, squad depth and tactical analysis
highlights:
# Curacao World Cup 2026: Fixtures, manager, squad depth and tactical analysis
[...]
Get all the latest Curacao stats as the tournament unfolds plus the latest squad, manager and fixture information for the South American side here.
[...]
Former PSV, Rangers and Sunderland manager Dick Advocaat was the man to lead Curacao to the World Cup but he resigned in February 2026 due to health problems with his daughter. These improved in May 2026 and this allowed Advocaat to return to the fold as head coach.. Curacao won all four of their games in Round Two, including beating Haiti 5-1. In Round Three, they won three and drew three of their six group matches, with their standout result a 7-0 victory away at Bermuda.
[...]
As mentioned, Curacao will face Germany, the Ivory Coast and Ecuador at the 2026 World Cup.
[...]
The nation open against Germany in Houston, before heading to Kansas City to take on Ecuador. The Blue Wave will then finish up Group E against the Ivory Coast in Philadelphia.

Although he didn’t pick up any bookings, Shurandy Sambo was a tackling machine during World Cup qualifying. No Curacao player averaged more than his 4.8 tackles per 90 minutes, which was second only to Guatemala’s Jose Rosales (5.5) across the entire qualifying campaign. Sambo also averaged two fouls per 90, and the Sparta Rotterdam loanee will need to call upon all of his defensive instincts and aggression against the likes of Germany and the Ivory Coast.
[...]
Curacao played a 3-4-3 formation during World Cup qualifying, with FC Zurich’s Livano Comenencia sitting deep in midfield to give the Bacuna brothers and wing-backs licence to push forward. There’s plenty of experience in the ranks, with the Bacunas on 114 caps combined and goalkeeper Eloy Room on 68. Meanwhile, title-winning PSV defender Amando Obispo is a quality new addition to the ranks, having previously represented the Netherlands at youth level.
[...]
The highly experienced Dick Advocaat is back in charge of Curacao. The former Sunderland manager was in charge of the team from January 2024 to February 2026 and lost just three of his 20 matches at the helm. However, he left the job in February 2026, citing personal reasons. These have since been resolved and Advocaat has returned to the head coach position at Curacao.
[...]
All of that experience will be put to the test this summer, when Advocaat leads the smallest nation at the World Cup into what looks like an impossible challenge.
[...]
Leandro Bacuna is expected to be Curacao’s captain at the World Cup.

results.title: 'Why not Curacao?' - Dick Advocaat believes in World Cup shock against Germany | Flashscore.com
highlights:
'Why not Curacao?' - Dick Advocaat believes in World Cup shock against Germany | Flashscore.com
[...]
# 'Why not Curacao?' - Dick Advocaat believes in World Cup shock against Germany
[...]
Curacao manager Dick Advocaat during Thursday's press conferenceROBIN VAN LONKHUIJSEN / ANP / AFP
[...]
Curaçao boss Dick Advocaat believes that the tournament newcomers could pull off a surprise against Germany in their World Cup opener.
[...]
"It's something special for us to be there. Playing against players you see on TV, who play in the top leagues. Anyone can surprise. Why not Curacao? That's what we'll try to do," said the 78-year-old on Thursday at the training camp in Noordwijk, the Netherlands.
[...]
Advocaat returned to his role as Curaçao manager after Fred Rutten stepped down just three months into his tenure, having replaced Advocaat, who left Curaçao to spend more time with his ailing daughter. Advocaat's return was reportedly demanded by sponsor Corendon and the players, shrouding his comeback in controversy.
[...]
"It’s been a difficult few weeks. A lot has happened," said Advocaat, whom the Curaçao Football Federation (FFK) said was only contacted after Rutten's departure.
[...]
"Things could have turned out differently. I haven’t been in touch with Rutten. Just for an hour when I handed over the reins. I didn’t hesitate to return. I can’t think of a reason why I would."
[...]
Now that the Dutchman is back, he can't wait to get started after feeling what it means to be the smallest nation to ever qualify for the World Cup.
[...]
"Reaching the next round is our goal," he said.
[...]
"It’s unprecedented for Curaçao. There’s a huge buzz about it. The joy of those people is so beautiful. We in the Netherlands could take a leaf out of their book. We’re looking forward to it."
[...]
On June 14, the team from the Caribbean island will face Germany in Houston for their opening match of the World Cup in the USA, Mexico, and Canada. In Group E, which also includes Ivory Coast and Ecuador, Curaçao are considered clear underdogs.
[...]

results.title: Leandro Bacuna on Advocaat's advice and Curaçao's cohesion
highlights:
Curaçao captain Leandro Bacuna talks about their FIFA World Cup 2026 campaign, growing up in a football family and underdog mentality.
[...]
It will be handsomely rewarded in the FIFA World Cup 2026™, as the smallest nation to qualify introduce themselves to the world in Group E against Côte d'Ivoire, Ecuador and Germany. The 34-year-old midfielder and captain spoke to FIFA about what people can expect from the Caribbean side at this year’s global finals.
[...]
Leandro Bacuna: It's a very nice story. It's a small island [that believes] in big achievements. [We believe] that we can build on something. When I came about ten years ago, we started building on reaching the World Cup. It was a dream, and the
[...]
actually came true.
[...]
He brought a lot to us. We like to party, we like to have fun, and he basically said: "Don't lose that, but make sure you play for the result." And I think that that's a very important message that he gave to us. At the end of the games we were still trying to win a game, and that maybe one point instead could help you in the future, and he brought that to us. He gave us so much confidence that we could actually believe in it, and we had the belief. We just needed that final touch.
[...]
Coming together. In life, you have people that don't believe in you. In Curaçao, they actually believed in it. We had a new president come in, and his first thing he said was, "We're going to reach the World Cup." He didn't make it come true – at the end of the day, it's the players that are playing – but it's people believing in you, and I think the day we qualified, we came together, and I saw all of the people together – enemies, everything – coming together as friends, hugging each other.
[...]
Tough question. I think yeah, of course. We are there for the first time, but I have to say that we are not afraid of anyone. We are going to go there, we are going to do our thing, and we're going to play our game and just enjoy the moment. But with enjoyment, you have to represent your country as well. We don’t want to go there and get (beaten) 7-0, 4-0, 5-0, lose every single game. We want to go and show what we can actually do and why we achieved our goal.
[...]
That it's a team. It's not about individuals: it's about everyone together. Not only the players, the people around as well: the staff members. We've got a big staff, but everyone has a job and everyone is helping in their way. So, it's about togetherness, it's about showing people what a small nation can actually do.
